newsitem.title: LATVIA: SECURITIES COMMISSION SEES COUNCIL APPROVED SOON.
newsitem.headline: SECURITIES COMMISSION SEES COUNCIL APPROVED SOON.

text.p: The securities commission said on Thursday that it hopes to see its council approved by parliament in a week and that half of its staff is already employed.
The securities commission is a state regulatory body to provide supervision of the Latvian equities market.
"I hope that parliament will decide on the candidatures in a week's time or so," Talis Laizans, deputy chairman of the committee, told Reuters.
The cooperation council of the government-forming factions on Wednesday approved five candidates to the committee nominated, by its chairman, Viktor Gustsons.
Gustsons list includes Ilmar Rimshevics, central bank vice president, Viktor Shadinov, privatisation agency legal manager and Ojar Kehris, head of the association of economists "2001".
The factions also approved Viktor Klauss, University of Latvia professor and Guntis Urlovskis, the Turiba cooperative movement finance manager.
"The board of the securities commission is already working, but there are law initiatives and some other matters for which we need the council's approval," Laizans said.
Gustsons, former president of the Balta Insurance company, was approved to the post of chairman late last year. Laizans, deputy chairman, is a former head of treasury at the Latvian Investment Bank.
